sources.title: Central Limit Theorem for Sequential Monte Carlo Methods and its Application to Bayesian Inference
sources.author: Nicolas Chopin
sources.read_status: Complete reading of the cited theorem statements, derivations and proofs. PDF pp. 4-10 cover the general SMC construction, CLT Theorems 1-2 and variance recursions; Appendix A.1 proof is PDF pp. 16-20; static-parameter SIR and stability results are PDF pp. 11-15, with Theorems 4-5 proofs in Appendix A.3-A.4, PDF pp. 21-26.
anchors: §§2.1-2.2, PDF pp. 3-7: mutation-correction-selection SMC, target/proposal weights, SIR and resample-move cases.
§2.3 and Theorems 1-2, PDF pp. 7-9: recursive asymptotic variance, recursively defined weighted 2+delta moment class, multinomial and residual resampling CLTs.
Appendix A.1, PDF pp. 16-20: induction proof of Theorem 1 using conditional CLTs and moment/Lindeberg bounds; residual proof route for Theorem 2.
§§3.1-3.2 and Theorem 4, PDF pp. 11-13: static parameter SIS/SIR asymptotic variance divergence under regular parametric conditions.
§3.3 and Theorem 5, PDF pp. 14-15; Appendix A.3-A.4, PDF pp. 21-26: sufficient stability assumptions and proof.
limitations: Finite-time CLTs are for the stated function class and a fixed horizon; they are not uniform-in-time statements.

Theorem 5 requires bounded test-function variation, uniformly bounded transition/proposal density ratios, and likelihood bounded above and bounded away from zero. The paper describes these assumptions as strong and unrealistic in many noncompact settings.
The fixed-parameter SIR rate uses the paper's regular parametric assumptions and does not apply to arbitrary particle algorithms.

limitations: EnKF is an approximate Gaussian method at finite ensemble size for nonlinear problems; the linear Kalman limit is an ensemble-size limit.
A strong 3DVAR tracking bound requires contraction of the analysis-forecast map and bounded observation error.
The 4DVAR discussion does not supply a general continuous-optimization convergence theorem.
The 4DVAR optimizer is a point estimate/MAP formulation under the Gaussian model, not a posterior uncertainty representation.

checked_local_suppliers.limit: Kernel/Markov-law prerequisites exist, but there are no filtering, smoothing, Kalman, SMC, particle-MCMC or data-assimilation items.
RCD existence has its standard-Borel qualification; density normalization is only on finite positive normalizer fibres.
No general multivariate conditional-Gaussian theorem or SMC-specific CLT is present.
Existing factorization and solve results are for positive-definite systems; they do not establish singular-covariance pseudoinverse formulas.
Gaussian process finite-dimensional laws are defined, but no general posterior/conditional Gaussian theorem is supplied.
This is a finite-instance approximation-algorithm definition, not a general continuous optimizer or convergence theorem.

open_proof_obligations: Prove the joint-PSD/observed-SPD multivariate Gaussian conditional theorem locally; exclude singular observed covariance absent a range-qualified proof.
Require positive-definite forecast covariances for the standard RTS inverse or prove a singular support-compatible version.
Prove finite-horizon SMC CLT under the exact recursively defined moment class; the tutorial's cited CLT display is insufficient.
Keep Chopin's restrictive time-uniform stability conditions separate from finite-horizon convergence.
Prove the particle-Gibbs extended-target marginal and Gibbs conditional kernels locally; source-cited identities are not proof completion.
Place a generic continuous optimization prerequisite in Category 3 before any claimed 4DVAR numerical convergence result.
